stanzas: વૈષ્ણવજન તો તેને રે કહીયે, જે પીડ પરાઈ જાણે રે.
પરદુઃખે ઉપકાર કરે તોયે, મન અભિમાન ન આણે રે. — વૈષ્ણવ ૧.
સકળ લોકમાં સહુને વંદે, નિંદા ન કરે કેની રે.
વાચ કાછ મન નિશ્ચલ રાખે, ધન ધન જનની તેની રે. — વૈષ્ણવ ૨.
સમદ્રષ્ટિને તૃષ્ણા ત્યાગી, પરસ્ત્રી જેને માત રે.
જિહ્વા થકી અસત્ય ન બોલે, પરધન નવ ઝાલે હાથ રે.— વૈષ્ણવ ૩.
મોહ માયા વ્યાપે નહિ જેને, દ્રઢ વૈરાગ્ય જેના મનમાં રે.
રામ નામ શું તાળી રે વાગી, સકળ તિરથ તેના તનમાં રે. — વૈષ્ણવ ૪.
વણલોભી ને કપટ રહિત છે, કામ ક્રોધ નિવાર્યા રે.
ભણે નરસૈયો તેનું દર્શન કરતા, કુળ ઈકોતેર તાર્યા રે. — વૈષ્ણવ ૫.
Call him a man of Viṣṇu who knows the pain of others.
He does good to others in their sorrow, and even so lets no pride come into his mind. — Vaiṣṇava 1.
In all the world he bows to everyone; he speaks ill of no one.
He keeps speech, loins and mind steady: blessed, blessed is his mother. — Vaiṣṇava 2.
He looks on all with an equal eye and has given up craving; another's wife is his mother.
His tongue speaks no untruth; he lays no hand on another's wealth. — Vaiṣṇava 3.
Delusion and illusion do not take hold of him; firm detachment is in his mind.
His clap has struck to the name of Rāma; all the places of pilgrimage are in his body. — Vaiṣṇava 4.
He is without greed and without deceit; he has held off desire and anger.
Says Narsaiyo: in seeing him, seventy-one generations of the family were carried across. — Vaiṣṇava 5.
vaiṣṇavajana to tene re kahīye, je pīḍa parāī jāṇe re.
paraduḥkhe upakāra kare toye, mana abhimāna na āṇe re. — vaiṣṇava 1.
sakaḷa lokamāṁ sahune vaṁde, niṁdā na kare kenī re.
vāca kācha mana niścala rākhe, dhana dhana jananī tenī re. — vaiṣṇava 2.
samadraṣṭine tr̥ṣṇā tyāgī, parastrī jene māta re.
jihvā thakī asatya na bole, paradhana nava jhāle hātha re.— vaiṣṇava 3.
moha māyā vyāpe nahi jene, draḍha vairāgya jenā manamāṁ re.
rāma nāma śuṁ tāḷī re vāgī, sakaḷa tiratha tenā tanamāṁ re. — vaiṣṇava 4.
vaṇalobhī ne kapaṭa rahita che, kāma krodha nivāryā re.
bhaṇe narasaiyo tenuṁ darśana karatā, kuḷa īkotera tāryā re. — vaiṣṇava 5.

notes: Romanization: ISO 15919, letter for letter, so the inherent a is written even where Gujarati does not sound it (vaiṣṇavajana, pīḍa, māta, hātha, tiratha are said vaiṣṇavjan, pīḍ, māt, hāth, tirath); anusvara ં is ṁ (lokamāṁ, vaṁde, śuṁ), ળ is ḷ, ઋ-sign r̥; e and o without macrons (Gujarati has no short/long pair). Digits of the refrain numbers as 1-5. 're' is a filler/emphatic particle of the song, romanized and not translated.
refrain '— vaiṣṇava n.' is the repeat sign of the original (sing the first line again); kept as it stands.
line 2.2: vāca kācha mana, 'speech, kācha, mind'. kācha (Hindi kāchh) is the tucked-in end of the loincloth, standing for sexual restraint; 'loins' keeps the image. Some read it as 'deed' or 'body'.
line 3.1: the text writes samadraṣṭine as one word; it is samadraṣṭi ne 'equal-sighted and' (ne = 'and' here).
line 4.2: 'rāma nāma śuṁ tāḷī vāgī', literally 'a clap (tāḷī) has sounded with the name of Rāma': an idiom for being wholly attuned to, absorbed in, the name (as one claps in time to a hymn).
line 4.1: moha and māyā, 'infatuation / delusion' and 'illusion / worldly attachment'.

line 5.2: Narsaiyo is the poet Narsinh Mehta's signature name (the bhaṇe 'says' formula). 'kuḷa īkotera', seventy-one generations of a family, saved (carried across the ocean of rebirth); whose family is not said: the seer's, by the usual reading.
Gujarati is translated plainly; 'a man of Viṣṇu' renders vaiṣṇavajana (a devotee of Viṣṇu). The dropped spaces and punctuation of the text are kept in rom ('hātha re.— vaiṣṇava 3.').
